EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East experienced a major escalation as Iran declared the closure of the Strait of Hormuz after attacking a commercial vessel, prompting extensive US airstrikes against over 140 military targets across Iran. In response, Iran launched coordinated missile and drone attacks against US military facilities in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, and Oman, causing casualties and damage in several locations. The US affirmed its commitment to freedom of navigation in the Strait, while regional states condemned Iran's actions, heightening the risk of broader conflict.

IRAN
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz until further notice, citing "illegal movements" by foreign vessels, and confirmed striking the Cypriot-flagged commercial ship GFS Galaxy, disabling it and leaving one crew member missing. This followed extensive US military strikes targeting approximately 140 Iranian military objectives, including missile and drone sites, naval capabilities, ammunition storage, and communication networks, primarily along the coast and in central Iran, with over 300 targets hit in the past three days. Casualties include Hamid-Reza Dehqan, a naval air defense officer, killed in US attacks in Jask, and two individuals injured in a strike on a communications tower in Kerman province. Critical infrastructure sustained widespread damage, with Iran's power company, Tavanir, reporting a 4,200 MW reduction in electricity capacity, over 2,000 damaged network points, and estimated losses exceeding 60 trillion Tomans due to "enemy aggression." A missile booster also struck a residential building in Dorood, Lorestan, causing material damage but no casualties. In retaliation, Iran launched missile and drone attacks against US military facilities across the Gulf region, including bases in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, and Oman, employing ballistic missiles such as the Qadr, Emad, Kheibar Shekan, Fateh-110, and Zolfaghar. Internally, the Supreme Leader's advisor, Mohsen Rezaei, and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, warned the US to honor agreements or face consequences, while hardline media celebrated the death of US Senator Lindsey Graham. The Supreme Leader's son, Mojtaba Khamenei, issued a written message vowing revenge for his father's death.

ISRAEL
The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) conducted an airstrike in southern Lebanon against Hezbollah operatives observed transporting anti-tank missiles into a building within Israel's buffer zone, with secondary explosions indicating significant ordnance. The 551st Brigade completed its seventh combat rotation in southern Lebanon, reportedly eliminating over 80 terrorists and destroying more than 200 terror infrastructures. The Israeli home front experienced a mistaken missile warning in Bnei Brak, attributed by the IDF to a technical glitch by the Cellcom cellular provider, not a security incident. Politically, the government extended the "special situation in the home front" until July 28. Defense Minister Yoav Gallant is reportedly preparing the IDF for an independent military operation against Iran, asserting that Iran's nuclear program has been halted due to Israeli actions. Minister Gallant also claimed Israel applied the "Rafah model" to southern Lebanon, resulting in the extensive destruction of 24 border villages, 15,000-20,000 homes, and approximately 90% of buildings. Prime Minister Netanyahu is considering attending Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral, which could include a meeting with President Trump. Senior political figures, including Gadi Eisenkot and Dan Illouz, expressed opposition to or departed the Likud party over the conscription law, which was approved in committee to freeze arrests of Haredi yeshiva students.

GAZA & WEST BANK
An Israeli drone strike reportedly hit the "Beit Afaina" factory in Gaza City, causing multiple casualties. In the West Bank, four Israeli settlers were arrested for assaulting a CNN news crew. IDF forces responded to a report of gunfire directed at an Israeli civilian in the Al-Mu'ayir and Khirbat Abu Falih areas of the Binyamin Brigade, initiating searches for suspects. A soldier and two Israeli women were safely extracted from Jericho after entering the city. Hamas called for protests in Sweden against Israeli actions in Gaza.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operatives were observed transporting anti-tank missiles into a building within the southern Lebanon buffer zone, prompting an Israeli airstrike that resulted in secondary explosions. A monument commemorating South Lebanon Army (SLA) soldiers in Metula was vandalized, with the Lebanese flag removed, and two IDF soldiers were identified as responsible for the act. Lebanese officials informed the US of their intent to participate in direct negotiations with Israel in Rome, emphasizing that the delegation would be diplomatic-only, without military representation. Al-Mayadeen reported that no date has been set for the "pilot zones" mechanism, with the Lebanese Army refusing direct coordination with the IDF and insisting on IDF withdrawal before entering any such zones.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Iraqi Prime Minister, Ali Al-Zaidi, is scheduled to visit Washington on Monday to finalize several energy agreements with the US. An Iraqi government spokesperson clarified that no foreign military bases exist in Iraq, only international advisors present at the government's request. Iraq's Foreign Ministry expressed concern over escalating maritime tensions in the region, stressing the need to respect national sovereignty. In an internal security development, the Ninawa criminal court sentenced a terrorist to death for converting a workshop into an explosives depot and carrying out assassinations in Mosul.

GULF STATES
The Gulf region experienced significant escalations. Oman summoned the Iranian Ambassador to protest drone attacks on its Musandam and Al Wusta provinces, while the US embassy in Muscat issued a security warning for Duqm and Musandam, advising citizens to shelter in place. Qatar announced a temporary suspension of all marine vessel activity for public safety and declared four days of national mourning following the death of its former Emir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, at age 74. Qatar also reported three injuries, including one child, from shrapnel due to Iranian missile interceptions. Kuwait condemned Iranian attacks on its territory as a "dangerous escalation" and reported its military engaging incoming aerial targets. Bahrain activated air raid sirens across the country and reported explosions, including one at the US Fifth Fleet base in Juffair. The United Arab Emirates (UAE) confirmed identifying missile threats but stated they were outside its borders, maintaining that the situation remains stable with national air defense systems on high alert. Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz reportedly plummeted by 90% after Iran's declared closure.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  Iran's IRGC declared the closure of the Strait of Hormuz after attacking the Cypriot-flagged commercial ship GFS Galaxy, disabling it and leaving one crew member missing.
2.  The US Central Command (CENTCOM) conducted extensive airstrikes, hitting approximately 140 military targets across Iran, marking the third round of strikes this week, bringing the total to over 300 targets.
3.  Iran retaliated with coordinated missile and drone strikes targeting US military facilities in Jordan (Prince Hassan Air Base), Kuwait (Al-Shuaikh Port, radar site), Bahrain (US Fifth Fleet HQ in Juffair), Qatar (Al Udeid Air Base), and Oman (Port of Duqm, Musandam province).
4.  Oman summoned the Iranian Ambassador to protest drone attacks on its territory, while Qatar reported 3 injuries from Iranian missile shrapnel, and Bahrain activated air raid sirens amid explosions at the US Fifth Fleet base.
5.  Hamid-Reza Dehqan, an Iranian naval air defense officer, was killed in US attacks in Jask, and Iran's power infrastructure sustained significant damage, with a reported 4,200 MW capacity reduction.
6.  Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped by 90%, with only 11 commercial vessels (8 tankers, 3 cargo ships) recorded in the last 24 hours.
7.  US Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch pro-Israel and anti-Iran voice, passed away at age 71, leading to condolences from US and Israeli leaders and celebratory remarks from Iranian media.
8.  Israel's Defense Minister indicated the IDF is preparing for an independent military operation against Iran and claimed extensive destruction in south Lebanon resembling the "Rafah model."

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are extremely high. The direct exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, particularly Iran's declaration of Hormuz closure and its retaliatory strikes against multiple US and allied bases in the Gulf, signal a significant shift towards open regional conflict. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, now a declared no-go zone by Iran with severely reduced commercial traffic, and the Gulf states, which are experiencing direct Iranian missile and drone attacks. Military postures have notably changed, with Iran broadening its retaliation geographically and militarily, and the US reaffirming its commitment to freedom of navigation in the Strait. Red lines, previously understood as limited engagements, appear to have been crossed by both sides, with Iran's direct targeting of commercial shipping and US bases, and the US's widespread punitive strikes. The Iranian Supreme Leader's son's vow for "certain" revenge for his father's death, coupled with calls from hardline Iranian media to attack Israel, indicates further potential for horizontal and vertical escalation, specifically involving Israel.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** has strongly condemned Iran's actions, with CENTCOM declaring the Strait of Hormuz remains open and US forces are ready to ensure freedom of navigation despite Iranian "aggression." Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated Iran made a "bad choice" and is now "paying the price." President Trump threatened massive retaliation against Iran with "a thousand missiles" if any attempt is made on his life, a threat US Ambassador Huckabee confirmed was based on Israeli intelligence.
Among **Gulf States**, Oman summoned the Iranian Ambassador to protest drone attacks on its territory, and its Maritime Security Center coordinated the rescue of crew from the attacked GFS Galaxy. Qatar has halted all marine vessel activity due to security concerns and reported injuries from Iranian missile shrapnel. Kuwait condemned Iranian attacks as "dangerous escalation" and is actively engaging aerial targets. The UAE confirmed detecting missile threats but stated they were outside its borders and its systems are on high alert.
**Pakistan's** Foreign Minister urged de-escalation, restraint, and diplomacy, emphasizing the June 2026 Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in a call with his Iranian counterpart.
**Israel's** Prime Minister Netanyahu, President Herzog, Defense Minister Gallant, and Foreign Minister Saar offered strong condolences on the death of US Senator Lindsey Graham, highlighting his unwavering support for Israel.
**France** saw the evacuation of 300 people in Sarcelles after weapons were found near a synagogue, though the incident's motive is unclear.
**Ukraine** reported striking 14-28 Russian ships in the Black Sea and Azov, including tankers, and hitting the Syzran oil refinery in Russia with drones.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz; Iran declares it closed, while US, UK maritime authorities, and Oman state the southern passage remains open, despite a reported 90% drop in commercial traffic. Iranian reporting on casualties and damage from US strikes (one naval officer killed, two injured, extensive power grid damage) may be incomplete given the scale of US operations against over 140 targets. The identity of the masked figure at Ali Khamenei's funeral remains ambiguous, with initial rumors of Mojtaba Khamenei now contradicted by Iranian media identifying him as a grandson, Muhammad Javad Khamenei, citing burn injuries, further clouding Mojtaba's public status despite his written vow for revenge. Iran's direct targeting of mediating Gulf states (Oman and Qatar) during diplomatic efforts to manage the Hormuz situation indicates a calculated disregard for de-escalation channels. Unverified claims include reports of explosions near the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant and widespread drone sightings over Tehran. Iranian state media's celebratory reporting on Senator Lindsey Graham's death serves as a clear propaganda indicator aimed at both domestic and external audiences. A notable reporting gap exists in detailed, independently confirmed assessments of the damage and casualties from both US and Iranian strikes, particularly within Iran and at US bases in the Gulf. Minister Gallant's claim of applying a "Rafah model" in south Lebanon, resulting in 90% destruction of 24 villages, is a very strong and potentially exaggerated claim that requires independent verification.
